root_cause.text: The mlx5e TC offload cleanup code incorrectly assumed every `MLX5_MAX_PORTS` slot had a valid peer `struct mlx5_eswitch`, so `mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peers_flow()`/`mlx5e_tc_clean_fdb_peer_flows()` iterated over non-existent devcom peers and dereferenced invalid peer flow lists during deletion.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `for (i = 0; i < MLX5_MAX_PORTS; i++)` with `mlx5_devcom_for_each_peer_entry(devcom, peer_esw, pos)` and derives `i = mlx5_get_dev_index(peer_esw->dev)`, and the crash occurs in `mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peers_flow()` with a NULL pointer dereference while deleting TC steering flows.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace fixed port-based peer flow deletion with iteration over actual devcom peers to correctly delete only existing peer flows.
intent_record.what: In mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peers_flow(), the code removed the fixed for-loop over all possible ports and replaced it with iteration over devcom peer entries. It now declares devcom, pos, and peer_esw, retrieves devcom from flow->priv->mdev->priv.eswitch->devcom, iterates with mlx5_devcom_for_each_peer_entry(devcom, peer_esw, pos), derives i from mlx5_get_dev_index(peer_esw->dev), and calls mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peer_flow(flow, i) for each peer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, peer flow deletion is now driven by the actual set of registered devcom peers instead of assuming every non-local port exists. This avoids attempting to delete flows for nonexistent peers and ensures only real peer eswitch devices are processed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch peer-flow cleanup to iterate over devcom peer eswitches so the correct peer flow lists are deleted.
intent_record.what: The function mlx5e_tc_clean_fdb_peer_flows() was changed from iterating over all port indices with a manual skip of the current device index to iterating over peer eswitch entries via devcom. Two new local pointers, devcom and pos, and a peer_esw pointer were added; devcom is assigned from esw->devcom, and the loop now uses mlx5_devcom_for_each_peer_entry(devcom, peer_esw, pos) to obtain each peer's device index before walking and deleting the corresponding peer_flows list.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup now targets peer flows based on the actual connected peer eswitch devices rather than assuming a fixed MLX5_MAX_PORTS index range and excluding only the local device. This makes peer-flow cleanup follow devcom-managed peer relationships, which can prevent missing or incorrectly addressing peer flow lists when the topology is not represented by a simple port loop.

grouping_result.intent: Switch peer-flow cleanup to iterate over devcom peer eswitches so the correct peer flow lists are deleted.

consistency_review.core_intent: Switch peer-flow cleanup from fixed port-based deletion to iterating over actual devcom peer eswitches so the correct peer flow lists are deleted.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they replace incorrect fixed MLX5_MAX_PORTS-based peer flow cleanup with iteration over actual devcom peer eswitches, preventing deletion of non-existent peers and invalid flow list dereferences.

candidates.rationale: This fixed-size loop assumes every port slot exists as a valid peer eswitch. That assumption is the root cause: it iterates over non-existent devcom peers and can lead to invalid peer-flow cleanup.
This statement deletes peer flows based on the loop index rather than actual existing peers, so it can dereference invalid peer flow lists when the assumed peer does not exist.
This loop has the same flawed assumption in the cleanup path: it walks all possible ports instead of only real peer eswitches, which can access invalid peer_flows entries.
This dereferences the per-port peer_flows list for every MLX5_MAX_PORTS slot, including non-existent peers, directly matching the invalid list access described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fixed-size loop iterates over all possible ports instead of only real devcom peers, which is the root cause of the invalid peer-eswitch and peer-flow-list access during cleanup.
This call deletes peer flows by port index from the flawed loop, so it can operate on non-existent peers and dereference invalid peer flow lists.

This cleanup iteration directly accesses the per-port peer_flows list for every MLX5_MAX_PORTS slot, including slots without valid peer eswitches, causing the invalid list dereference described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the cleanup code iterating over every MLX5_MAX_PORTS slot and assuming each slot has a valid peer eswitch. In this commit, that logic has already been changed to per-peer handling: cleanup now loops over ports with `for (i = 0; i < MLX5_MAX_PORTS; i++)`, skips the local device with `if (i == mlx5_get_dev_index(esw->dev)) continue;`, and iterates `esw->offloads.peer_flows[i]` instead of a single global list. Likewise, deletion was split into `mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peers_flow()` and `mlx5e_tc_del_fdb_peer_flow(flow, peer_index)`, and the latter only deletes matching peer entries (`if (peer_index != mlx5_get_dev_index(peer_flow->priv->mdev)) continue;`) before clearing DUP only when `list_empty(&flow->peer_flows)`. This indicates the old unsafe assumption is no longer present, so the function body already contains the fix.
